title: Design of 1.55‑μm InGaAlAs MQW High‑Saturation‑Power Semiconductor Optical Amplifiers for Space Optical Communications via Self‑Consistent Traveling‑Wave Thermal‑Optical Simulation
content: Free-space optical communication (FSOC) links are constrained by stringent power budgets, which high-power booster semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) can relax directly. This study presents a systematic pre-fabrication theoretical design of 1.55-μm InGaAlAs multiple-quantum-well (MQW) SOAs with ultra-high saturation output power. A self-consistent travelling-wave model solves the carrier rate equation, the interband gain, the longitudinal power propagation and a lumped thermal network simultaneously, treating gain saturation and thermal roll-over on the same footing. The model is verified by mesh-convergence and energy-balance tests and by comparison with published transparency carrier density, differential gain and thermal-resistance values. The influences of well thickness (5.2–7.0 nm), well number (2–6) and cavity length (1–5 mm) on the saturation output power are then investigated. The well number and cavity length, rather than the well thickness, dominate the power performance: for a 5-mm cavity with 2–3 wells, an on-chip saturation output power above 700 mW is predicted, with the junction temperature rise kept below 13 K at 3 W dissipated power by p-side-down AlN/Cu mounting. Design guidelines and a benchmark against reported high-power 1.55-μm amplifiers are provided, supplying a quantitative parameter window for high-saturation-power SOAs dedicated to space optical communication; experimental verification is ongoing.
